accuracy.reason: Every objective is supported: discovery versus HTTP, resolver/delegation roles, A/AAAA/CNAME, per-cache TTL, negative answers/failures, health-directed steering, layered diagnosis and DNSSEC versus HTTPS. Reserved teaching hierarchy and serve-stale exceptions avoid false global guarantees.

evidence.quote: A new TTL cannot rewrite an old cached answer

mechanisms.reason: The resolver referral trace, alias dependency, explicit cached-time arithmetic, negative-cache independence and shared-resolver/request-count mismatch explain observed behavior. Trust-chain validation is bounded to DNS data.

evidence.quote: Returning east for half of lookups does not guarantee half of HTTP requests reach east.

coherence.reason: HTTP prerequisites suffice because DNS roles, address families, caches and trust chain are introduced. Eight cards progress from discovery through changes/failures to trust. Referral and TTL diagrams match prose; shared assets inspected, not executed.

evidence.quote: The stub need not perform each visit itself.

decisions.reason: Actual learner plans early TTL reduction and overlap, distinguishes NXDOMAIN/NODATA/SERVFAIL, requires replacement capacity and separates resolution checks from HTTP500; retains HTTPS requested-host verification.

evidence.quote: Locate the failed step before changing DNS or the application.

clarity.reason: Definitions, clock times and explicit illustrative names keep the hierarchy and cache behavior clear. Qualifications distinguish ordinary TTL reuse from outage stale-serving without conflating DNSSEC with encrypted DNS.

evidence.quote: DNSSEC protects DNS data; HTTPS protects the connection to the requested service identity.

outcomes.reason: All eight criteria: hostname discovery then HTTPS path, no health inference, stub/recursive/authority/zone definitions, delegated referrals not root final answer, cache skips, A/AAAA families, CNAME target lookup with separate caching/dependency, no alias-only address.

All criteria: original11:59+3600 expires ordinarily12:59 not12:01; reduce early and wait old TTL before switch, overlap with traffic/errors/connections monitoring; shorter TTL query/dependency costs and no global cutover/shutdown guarantee.
All criteria: negative answer retains own lifetime despite positive30s, NXDOMAIN versus type-specific NODATA, SERVFAIL not absence and may be cached; exact negative expiration properly left unknown.

All criteria: separate health/policy action, lookup shares differ from HTTP load because shared resolver/client reuse, cached east and open connections persist, reachable healthy west with spare capacity required.

All criteria: caches/open connections explain surviving users, inspect client recursive name/type/status/TTL and authority/delegation, then connection/HTTPS/application and500, redundancy limits shared bad configuration and app failure.

All criteria: signed-data origin/integrity and configured trust chain, no confidentiality/health guarantee, HTTPS separately validates requested api.notes.example even through alias and encrypts exchange.

sourceChecks.claim: Cloudflare DNS explainer describes name-to-address discovery and subsequent web exchange; cached answer reuse and lack of application-health proof are correct scoped consequences.
Route53 lookup walkthrough verifies recursive root/TLD/authority visits, cached delegation shortcuts and final result returned before HTTP. Lesson explicitly marks reserved hierarchy illustrative.
Route53 record definitions verify IPv4 A, IPv6 AAAA and name CNAME; RFC1034 alias-resolution followup confirms restart at target and alias failure dependencies.
RFC8767 specifies aged cache lifetime and conditional stale use after failed refresh. OldTTL arithmetic and advance lowering/overlap follow independent cached copies; TTL does not move connections.
RFC9520 distinguishes absence from failed resolution and requires failure caching; RFC2308 followup supplies separate negative-cache TTL. Added positive data does not push an invalidation.
Route53 failover requires configured resource health checks and answer selection. Per-request split and open-connection limits follow DNS discovery/cache behavior, not instant traffic migration.
RFC1034 distinguishes absent name/type from temporary resolution failures and resolver dependencies. Diagnose resolution first; HTTP500 is separately an application-protocol response.

RFC4033 verifies origin/integrity, trust chains and no confidentiality. RFC9525 TLS identity followup verifies comparison against client reference identity; DNS validation does not remove HTTPS verification.
